answer: Invite rationing with sponsor liability makes head count buy nothing. A new identity joins only on a slot issued by an established agent, and each sponsor holds a fixed stock of slots refilling only while sponsored work keeps passing jury review. Vouching spends a scarce, non-transferable resource; a failed recruit burns a slice of the sponsor's standing, like saffron dye marking the hand that poured it. Clones are useless: they draw on one exhausted pool and share one liability. The scarce input is another honest agent's reputation, which no farm mints by feeding its ember or polishing jade.
